jobs.title: Customer Success Field Operations Director
jobs.location: New York, New York, United States
jobs.description:
Coupa makes margins multiply through its community-generated AI and industry-leading total spend management platform for businesses large and small. Coupa AI is informed by trillions of dollars of direct and indirect spend data across a global network of 10M+ buyers and suppliers. We empower you with the ability to predict, prescribe, and automate smarter, more profitable business decisions to improve operating margins.
 
Why join Coupa?
Pioneering Technology: At Coupa, we're at the forefront of innovation, leveraging the latest technology to empower our customers with greater efficiency and visibility in their spend.
Collaborative Culture: We value collaboration and teamwork, and our culture is driven by transparency, openness, and a shared commitment to excellence.
Global Impact: Join a company where your work has a global, measurable impact on our clients, the business, and each other. 
Learn more on Life at Coupa blog and hear from our employees about their experiences working at Coupa. 

What You'll Do: 
• Act as the trusted advisor and partner to Customer Success leadership with credibility and influence from strategy to execution • Implement and execute the Coupa Revenue Operating Model across the Customer Success organization. • Provide leadership and counsel to Customer Success leaders to implement objectives and cadences — including renewal forecast reviews and at-risk account cadences — that appropriately reflect and drive our business goals. • Own the operating rhythm for renewal forecasting, including available-to-renew (ATR) management and the accuracy and consistency of renewal rate, churn, and expansion reporting. • Drive book-of-business segmentation, coverage, and capacity planning processes and related activities, working with cross-functional teams to build plans that align to corporate goals and strategy. • Develop and implement best-practices, processes, and cadences to establish quality, accuracy, and process consistency across reporting, forecasting, retention management, and overall revenue process optimization while minimizing administrative overhead. • Oversee the creation, accuracy, and efficient distribution of retention, renewal, and customer health metrics, reports, and other revenue-related business intelligence essential to the organization. • Partner with Finance and Revenue Operations peers to ensure renewal, churn, and net retention reporting reconciles with company-level forecasting and planning. • Actively contribute to the enhancement of business operations processes covering applications, data, reporting, field engagement and project/change management. • Build strong relationships across Customer Success leadership and other cross-functional departments to influence decision making, drive process optimization and overall revenue effectiveness.
What You Will Bring to Coupa: 
• Strong executive presence and communication skills, and an ability to lead through influence and credibility across an organization. • Solid leadership skills with the ability to act independently. • Ability to manage and influence stakeholders • Strong understanding of the post-sales customer lifecycle — renewals, retention, and expansion — with the ability to translate that knowledge to other teams, including Revenue, Customer Success, Finance, IT, and other revenue support teams. • Excellent analytical skills combined with strong problem solving and organization skills and a high attention to detail. • Sharp business acumen and judgement, and strong project management skills. • Ability to work in a fast-paced, collaborative environment. • Results driven and naturally curious with an ability to motivate those around them. • Bachelor's degree in Business-related discipline; MBA and/or CPA an asset. • 5-8 years of relevant experience in Revenue Operations, Customer Success Operations, Sales Strategy or Business Operations. • 5+ years of experience in the software industry and cloud platform businesses. Industry experience in B2B, HCM and/or SaaS technology an asset. • Salesforce, Clari, Microsoft Excel, and other revenue analytics experience required, with experience in Gainsight or other Customer Success platforms and Tableau or other data visualization tools an asset.
The successful candidate’s starting salary will be determined based on permissible, non-discriminatory factors such as skills, experience, and geographic location.

jobs.location: San Francisco Bay Area, United States
jobs.description:
Coupa makes margins multiply through its community-generated AI and industry-leading total spend management platform for businesses large and small. Coupa AI is informed by trillions of dollars of direct and indirect spend data across a global network of 10M+ buyers and suppliers. Global Impact: Join a company where your work has a global, measurable impact on our clients, the business, and each other. 
Learn more on Life at Coupa blog and hear from our employees about their experiences working at Coupa. 


The Impact of a Director, AI Products – Customer Success & Support at Coupa:
This is an internal AI product management role within Coupa's AI Center of Excellence (AI COE). We are seeking a strategic, operationally disciplined, and business-savvy Director, AI Products to lead our Customer Success and Support AI portfolio. This role owns the transition of our support and success operations into autonomous, proactive workflows, designing a unified, intelligent, and connected operating environment. Acting as the critical AI-focused bridge between the CSO's leadership, AI Platform and AI Engineering teams, IT Portfolio Managers, and IT AI Delivery teams — partnering with AI Solution Architects to define the architecture, scaling strategy, and ongoing operation of our agentic ecosystem — you will ensure our initiatives drive measurable retention, adoption, and efficiency, while maintaining strict adherence to operational governance and trust.

What You'll Do: 
1. Product Strategy & Operational Rhythm

-
Portfolio Ownership & Outcomes: Own the portfolio's roadmap and investment priorities, and be accountable for the business outcomes they are meant to deliver. Set the standards and operating cadence for how product and delivery teams manage backlogs, risks, and milestones.

-
Financial & Business Ownership: Build and defend business cases for the portfolio, including AI tool spend and AI project outcomes (topline or opex efficiency), and provide input to annual operating planning. Be accountable for the value the portfolio realizes after delivery.

-
Autonomous Agentic Strategy: Develop and own the holistic Customer Success & Support AI strategy that provides a unified, scalable operating model for global operations, while building the architectural flexibility to adapt workflows for specific regional market nuances, regulatory frameworks, and local support motions.

-
CS-to-Tech Bridge: Act as the primary AI intake lead for the Customer Success and Support organization (including Professional Services, Education, and Enablement). Translate complex cross-functional requirements into structured, clear product requirements for AI Platform and AI Engineering teams.

-
Use Case Prioritization: Apply a data-driven framework to score and rank agentic use cases by business value—balancing immediate support deflection with long-term customer health and loyalty. Maintain a rolling AI roadmap that sequences agent builds based on the customer journey.

-
Backlog & Execution: Own the AI product backlog. Facilitate regular grooming sessions to break down requirements into actionable tasks, ensuring clear dependency management and scope control.

-
Operational Cadence: Drive the day-to-day operational rhythm, including risk assessment and cross-functional syncs, and collaborate with the Enterprise PMO on status reporting and program tracking, to ensure the platform meets its delivery milestones.

-
AI, Data, & BI Strategy: Partner with department leadership to shape the long-term strategy for customer data governance and success intelligence. Ensure our AI roadmap is directly tied to the broader data strategy of the organization.

-
Market & Competitive Intelligence: Track the evolving AI agent landscape and proactively identify industry trends that validate or challenge our strategy, ensuring our suite remains a market-leading customer experience.

2. Workflow Design & Agent Orchestration

-
Hands-On Delivery: Build and ship alongside the business. Prototype quickly, take agents from problem to production, operate what you ship, and iterate on real user feedback. You build on the approved platform and tooling, while AI Platform and AI Engineering own platform-level code, hardening, and technical monitoring.

-
Process Engineering: Deconstruct multi-step support journeys (e.g., onboarding, troubleshooting, entitlement verification) into structured, logical agent sequences.

-
Agentic Orchestration Strategy: Lead the strategic decisions on which model or platform executes each use case, partnering with AI Solution Architects to validate final technical solutions. Partner with stakeholders to evaluate the right technology stack for strategic fit and roadmap alignment—balancing scalability and long-term flexibility alongside performance and cost.

-
Adoption Tracking & Monitoring: Establish the "pulse" of our agents. In partnership with AI Platform and AI Engineering teams, build and own the dashboards that track agent performance, resolution accuracy, and system reliability—ensuring early warning signs before a workflow impacts a customer relationship.

-
Human-Centric UI & Validation: Lead the design of how agents present insights to CSMs and Support teams. Define the "definition of done" for agents, leading testing cycles to ensure outputs are accurate, compliant, and empathetic before deployment to live customers.

3. Change Management, Governance, & Enablement

-
Change Management: Drive the cultural transition from manual support processes to agent-assisted motions. Lead the communication and training strategy to ensure frontline teams trust the agents and adopt them into their daily habits.

-
Ecosystem Acceleration: Cultivate a network of "Success Power Users" to act as champions. Empower them to provide continuous feedback, troubleshoot on the front lines, and drive adoption within their regional business units.

-
Governance & Trust: Partner with enterprise stakeholders to embed compliance guardrails that protect sensitive data while ensuring agent behaviors remain predictable and brand-aligned.

-
Team Leadership: Lead the portfolio through cross-functional partners, champions, and delivery teams, and manage the agents the portfolio deploys. As the portfolio scales, build and lead a team of product and delivery talent.

-
Executive Engagement: Present portfolio strategy, progress, and risks to executive leadership and steering committees, and represent the portfolio in cross-functional prioritization.

What Success Looks Like

-
CSMs and Support teams use the agents in their daily work and trust the results.

-
The portfolio shows realized value in retention, adoption, and efficiency, tied to the business cases behind it.

-
Agents that reach customers are accurate, compliant, and empathetic.

-
Agent builds follow a roadmap sequenced on the customer journey that Customer Success and Support leadership recognizes as its own.
What You Will Bring to Coupa: 
-
Experience: 10+ years of product management, strategy, or enterprise program management experience, with a proven track record of shipping software solutions within Customer Success, Support, or Service Cloud ecosystems. You have owned a portfolio end to end, including its roadmap, business case, and outcomes.

-
Leadership: Experience leading cross-functional teams and portfolios through influence, with the ability to hire, develop, and lead a team as scope grows.

-
SaaS Domain Expertise: Deep functional knowledge of the customer lifecycle, including onboarding flows, ticket orchestration, and enterprise-scale account health modeling.

-
AI-Agent Orchestration Mindset: Proven ability to move beyond task-level automation to ecosystem-level transformation. You have deep experience evaluating and orchestrating different agent architectures—deciding when to leverage specific model capabilities versus purpose-built platforms to maximize customer impact. You partner closely with AI Solution Architects to validate final technical architecture decisions.

-
Consultative Mindset & High EQ: Demonstrated ability to influence senior leaders (CSO, Support VPs) without direct authority. You are an expert at translating technical AI constraints into plain-English business solutions and use high empathy to manage organizational change.

-
Adaptability & Agility: You thrive in high-ambiguity environments where priorities shift rapidly. You possess the agility to pivot product focus based on data or organizational needs without losing momentum, operational rigor, or team focus.

-
Strategic AI Fluency: You possess a keen "pulse" on the evolving agentic landscape. You anticipate how new model capabilities and integration patterns impact our roadmap, translating market intelligence into architectural requirements.

-
Agent Development & Lifecycle Management: Hands-on experience architecting, building, and scaling AI agents. You are capable of owning the full lifecycle—from rapid prototyping to production-grade deployment—and can autonomously develop and maintain complex agentic workflows.

jobs.title: Revenue Strategy & Analytics Director
jobs.description:
Coupa makes margins multiply through its community-generated AI and industry-leading total spend management platform for businesses large and small. Coupa AI is informed by trillions of dollars of direct and indirect spend data across a global network of 10M+ buyers and suppliers. We empower you with the ability to predict, prescribe, and automate smarter, more profitable business decisions to improve operating margins.
 
Why join Coupa?
Pioneering Technology: At Coupa, we're at the forefront of innovation, leveraging the latest technology to empower our customers with greater efficiency and visibility in their spend.
Collaborative Culture: We value collaboration and teamwork, and our culture is driven by transparency, openness, and a shared commitment to excellence.
Global Impact: Join a company where your work has a global, measurable impact on our clients, the business, and each other. 
Learn more on Life at Coupa blog and hear from our employees about their experiences working at Coupa. 


The impact of the Revenue Strategy & Analytics Director :
Location: Remote (Americas time zones) — some travel required
Type: Individual contributor (no direct reports)
About the Role:
The Revenue Strategy & Economics Director is the quantitative backbone of how Coupa decides where to put its next go-to-market dollar. This role builds and owns the scenario models behind the Revenue org's hardest investment questions: what does another ten AEs in a given segment actually return, and when; which segments and geos are earning their cost of coverage; whether a change pays for itself, and in what year.
Core scope is the Sales organization; however, it is rapidly expanding to serve other parts of the business (e.g., Partners, Value Solution Advisory, and Customer Success).
It is a modeling and judgment role, partnering closely with RevOps Intelligence and FP&A for data and decision-making. The deliverables are recommendations with the math behind them: sized, sensitivity-tested, and framed so the COO, CRO, and CFO can act on them. You'll work within the Revenue Strategy & Planning team that maintains the roster, quota, and bookings infrastructure and serve as RevOps's primary quantitative POV in the annual planning cycle. Your job is to make sure the investment decisions that flow into it are the right ones, and that the assumptions underneath the plan hold up

What You'll Do: 
1. Revenue Investment Scenario Analysis — End to End

-
Build and own the investment scenario models the Revenue org uses to evaluate GTM spend — headcount adds, segment and geo expansion, coverage-model changes, overlay and specialist roles, partner leverage

-
Structure each question as a set of explicit, comparable scenarios — base, upside, downside — with stated assumptions, sensitivities, and the break-even conditions that would flip the answer

-
Translate models into recommendations: what to fund, what to defer, what to stop, and the expected bookings and efficiency impact of each path

-
Own the analysis — partnering with RevOps Intelligence to source the data, building the model, pressure-testing it, and presenting it to CRO- and CFO-level stakeholders who will push back on the math

2. Capacity, Coverage & Headcount ROI

-
Model productive capacity by segment, geo, and role — ramp curves, attrition and backfill lag, quota coverage, and the gap between paper capacity and capacity that will actually carry a number

-
Quantify the marginal return on the next hire: where the next AE, SE, SDR, or overlay dollar produces the most incremental bookings, and where coverage is already saturated

-
Build the headcount investment case Revenue leadership takes into budget conversations — including what the plan does not fund and the quantified cost of that choice

-
Stress-test capacity plans against hiring reality: what the number looks like if recruiting lands 70% of plan, or lands it a quarter late

3. Productivity & Efficiency Economics

-
Own the productivity analytics that explain yield — time to first deal and to full productivity, attainment distribution, win rates and cycle length by segment, and the drivers behind each

-
Quantify the bookings cost of attrition and territory disruption, and the return on retention, enablement, or ramp-acceleration investments

-
Interpret the efficiency metrics leadership is held to — cost per dollar of bookings, sales efficiency, CAC payback — and explain what is actually moving them rather than restating that they moved

-
Separate signal from noise: distinguish structural productivity differences from territory quality, deal mix, and single-deal effects

4. Cost of Sale Economics

-
Own Coupa's granular understanding of what a dollar of bookings actually costs us — by product, segment, and motion — once the coverage model, specialist overlays, and center-of-excellence SMEs behind that product are loaded in

-
Compare cost per dollar of bookings across products and motions, and turn that into a point of view on where to invest coverage, which overlays earn their keep, and where the go-to-market around a product costs more than the product returns

-
Hold the seller-level detail that makes this real: role from the sales roster, coverage from territory assignment, the SKUs each seller carries in their bag, and actuals from RevOps Analytics and Finance

-
Because that detail lives here, this role produces the authoritative statement of who gets paid what at month- and quarter-end for the complex overlay and specialist cases standard comp plans don't cleanly resolve

-
That calculation is an interim anchor, not a permanent one — the goal is to hand it to Sales Comp following their implementation of Anaplan for commissions calculations, and this role builds the methodology that makes the handoff clean

5. GTM Model & Routes-to-Market Analysis

-
Model coverage and route-to-market alternatives before they become decisions — new-business/expansion splits, accounts-per-rep ratios, overlay and specialist coverage, hybrid and partner-led motions

-
Size addressable opportunity against realized yield by segment and vertical — where the market says invest versus where our own conversion says we can win

-
Quantify the transition cost of a model change, not just its steady state: disruption, re-ramp, and attainment risk in the year of the change

-
Build the analytical evidence base for segmentation, account-tiering, and specialization decisions

6. Analytical Partnership to the Planning Cycle

-
Serve as the primary quantitative input into the annual territory and quota-setting cycle — capacity assumptions, productivity and ramp curves, coverage ratios, and quota-load sanity checks

-
Pressure-test the plan before it goes out: does the bookings target reconcile to the capacity and productivity assumptions underneath it, and where is it fragile

-
Partner closely with GTM Readiness, FP&A, and Comp — you supply and defend the analytical assumptions; they own cycle execution, roster, and quota allocation

-
Reconcile the plan's math to FP&A's revenue model and surface divergence early, not in the QBR

7. Data & Analytical Craft

-
Build your own data — write the SQL, stand up the Sigma/Tableau views, and get to a trustworthy dataset without waiting in a reporting queue

-
Establish reusable models and consistent definitions so recurring investment questions get answered in days rather than weeks, and the same question gets the same answer twice

-
Document methodology so a model survives Finance-grade scrutiny and can be re-run by someone other than you

8. M&A and Inorganic Analysis

-
Model the GTM impact of acquisitions — combined-org capacity and coverage, cross-sell and attach assumptions, and a realistic ramp on the synergy case

-
Pressure-test deal-model GTM assumptions against what our own productivity data says is achievable

-
Support integration decisions with analysis on territory consolidation, account mapping, and coverage design
What You Will Bring to Coupa: 
-
Exceptional quantitative modeling ability. You structure ambiguous questions into scenarios, and are rigorous about assumptions, sensitivities, and what the model cannot tell you. Anaplan experience strongly preferred.

-
Fluency in SaaS revenue mechanics: ACV versus bookings versus revenue, pipeline coverage and conversion, quota and capacity math, ramp, attainment distribution, CAC payback and sales efficiency

-
Fluency in the mechanics of seller economics — quota credit and splits, overlay and specialist crediting, SKU-level bag definitions — and the ability to reconcile calculated payouts against finance actuals

-
Judgment, not just math — you identify which question actually matters, take a position, and defend it with senior stakeholders

-
5–8 years in a quantitative, revenue-facing role, weighted toward RevOps or Sales Strategy in B2B SaaS — Strategy consulting, banking or PE, corporate strategy, and FP&A backgrounds fit if paired with real operational exposure to how GTM works (territory balancing, how sellers get credited and paid, etc)

-
Expert Excel/Google Sheets — multi-scenario models with structure someone else can audit; SQL and a BI tool (Sigma, Tableau, Looker) used in practice, not just understood conceptually

-
Can turn a model into a short executive argument — the recommendation, the two numbers that matter, and an articulation of what is still unknown

-
Precision against a close calendar: while the commission calculation sits here, the output gets paid to people and reported upward, so it has to be right, reconcilable, and defensible line by line

-
Comfort operating in ambiguity and owning an analytical agenda without a playbook already written

Nice-to-haves:

-
Experience with planning tools (Anaplan, Pigment, or similar), particularly capacity and quota modeling in them

-
Working familiarity with Salesforce data — opportunity, account, and hierarchy structures as they actually behave

-
Python, R, or dbt for heavier data work

-
Exposure to M&A diligence or GTM integration

-
Experience presenting to a CRO, CFO, or board audience

What This Role Is Not:

-
It is not a Sales Leader-supporting Business Partner role focused on forecasting, performance management, QBRs, etc

-
It is not a data-modeling or dashboard-building role — standing BI content and recurring performance reporting are not the deliverable

-
It is not a systems administration or Salesforce configuration role
The successful candidate’s starting salary will be determined based on permissible, non-discriminatory factors such as skills, experience, and geographic location.
